task.description: Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0401. Read docs/issues/ISS-0401.yaml in full first. Symptom: test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:392-394's `assert function_exported?(Repository, :upsert_content, 6)` fails (returns false) even though lib/letflow/repository.ex:251 defines a genuinely public `upsert_content/6` with a matching @spec, confirmed present in the compiled module via `Letflow.Repository.__info__(:functions)` (which DOES show it). This is a real, reproducible discrepancy between `function_exported?/3` and `__info__(:functions)` for the same module/function/arity -- not a typo or a missing function. Reproduce it directly yourself first (do not trust the prior report's prose alone, per No Speculation): run `mix test test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:392` standalone and confirm the failure, then use `mix run -e` or an IEx-equivalent one-liner to directly compare `function_exported?(Letflow.Repository, :upsert_content, 6)` against `Letflow.Repository.__info__(:functions) |> Enum.filter(fn {n,_} -> n == :upsert_content end)` in the same BEAM session, to confirm the exact discrepancy. Root-cause it: the most likely explanation (per the issue's own filing note) is that `function_exported?/3` requires the target module to already be *loaded* into the VM (not merely compiled to a .beam on disk), and returns false for a compiled-but-not-yet-loaded module, while `__info__(:functions)` implicitly triggers a load as a side effect of being called -- but verify this is actually what's happening (e.g. by checking `:code.is_loaded(Letflow.Repository)` before and after the assertion, or by adding a deliberate `Code.ensure_loaded?/1` call ahead of the assertion and confirming that alone fixes it) rather than assuming. Also check whether this is specific to test run order/parallelism (does it fail when this test file is run alone vs. as part of the full suite; does test order within the file matter) since the original filing noted uncertainty about test-ordering interaction. Do NOT implement the fix -- produce a diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER (or determine directly, if the fix is truly a one-line `Code.ensure_loaded?/1` guard with no design decision to make, whether this qualifies for ORCH's own direct-action sizing rule per docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10 -- state your assessment either way in the diagnosis, but the routing decision itself is ORCH's, not yours).
